nodes.title: Gaussian elimination as a product of row operations

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $m$ and $n$ be finite linearly ordered sets, and let $A$ be an $m \times n$ matrix over $K$. Then there are an $m \times n$ matrix $R$ over $K$ in reduced row echelon form and an invertible $m \times m$ matrix $P$ over $K$ with $R = PA$. In other words, $A$ is row-equivalent to a matrix in reduced row echelon form.

nodes.title: One pivot step of Gaussian elimination

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $m$ and $n$ be finite linearly ordered sets, and let $R_1$ and $R_2$ be $m \times n$ matrices over $K$ in reduced row echelon form. If $R_2 = P R_1$ for some invertible $m \times m$ matrix $P$ over $K$, then $R_1 = R_2$. In other words, a row-equivalence class contains at most one matrix in reduced row echelon form.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the reduced row echelon form

nodes.summary: Let $K$ be a field, let $m$ and $n$ be finite sets, let $A$ be an $m \times n$ matrix over $K$, and let $P$ be an invertible $m \times m$ matrix over $K$. Then the linear maps $x \mapsto PAx$ and $x \mapsto Ax$ on $K^n$ have the same kernel; that is, the homogeneous systems $PAx = 0$ and $Ax = 0$ have the same solutions.
nodes.title: Invertible row operations preserve the null space

nodes.summary: Let $R$ be a type with elements $0$ and $1$, and let $A$ be a matrix over $R$ in reduced row echelon form whose rows are indexed by a linearly ordered set and whose columns are indexed by a linearly ordered set $N$. Let $e : O \to N$ be an order isomorphism from a linearly ordered set $O$. Then the matrix $B$ with columns indexed by $O$ and entries $B_{ik} = A_{i\,e(k)}$ is in reduced row echelon form.
nodes.title: Order-preserving reindexing of columns preserves reduced row echelon form
